blocks.title: Honors — finish the string
blocks.markdown: Yesterday the two-string demo broke the room's prediction. Today we close the loop on it — not by re-watching, but by making the **assumptions** in your inertia explanation explicit. A model that can't say *when it would break* isn't finished.

## State your assumptions (and when they'd break)

Your Day 1 explanation — *the jerk loads the bottom string faster than the mass's inertia lets it accelerate, so the force never reaches the top* — quietly assumes things. Good physicists name them.

What the explanation assumes:
- The strings are **identical** (same breaking strength). If the top string were secretly weaker, the result could flip — and it would no longer be an inertia story at all.
- The pull on a **jerk** rises to the breaking force *faster* than the mass can begin moving. Pull slowly enough and the mass has time to accelerate, passing the load up — the **top** breaks instead.
- The mass is **rigid** and the string **massless** — all the resistance comes from the hanging mass's inertia, not from stretch in the string.

*A claim with no stated limits is just a guess that got lucky.*

blocks.title: When the model breaks
blocks.markdown: If you pulled the bottom string **slowly** but still saw it snap, your inertia explanation would be in trouble. Naming that failure condition *in advance* is what separates a defended claim from a memorized one.

blocks.frame: The same rig breaks differently because of inertia — the mass resists ___. This explanation depends on the assumption that ___, and it would FAIL if ___.
blocks.prompt: JUSTIFY: Explain why the two-string rig breaks differently depending on how you pull, using inertia. Then name ONE assumption your explanation depends on and describe the observation that would prove the explanation wrong.

blocks.title: Connect forward
blocks.markdown: **Mass resists change in motion.** That single sentence is the obstacle the whole year fights. 2026-XJ has an enormous mass, so it has enormous inertia — it will not be nudged easily. Every unit from here is one long attempt to move it anyway.
